about_hero_desc: A project born from passion for Pokemon Unite and competitive esports. Built by a player, for players who want to improve seriously.
about_creator_body:
I'm Fizzey, a competitive Pokemon Unite player and passionate web developer. An active member of the French esport scene, I created Unite Tools to fill the gap in quality tools for our community.

My goal: make competitive resources accessible to everyone in the same place, for free, without compromising on quality.
about_quote: "My goal is to create a tool for the competitive community that I and my team will also use."
about_why_body:
The competitive Pokemon Unite scene was sorely lacking dedicated tools. No updated online draft simulator, no damage calculator, nothing to practice map control.

Unite Tools was born from that frustration. A solo project, built with passion, to raise the level of the entire community and beyond.
about_team_desc: Beyond building this site, I'm a player for Volticons Unite, a European team qualified in the official Pokemon Unite league.

map_timer_htu_title: How to use the Map Timer
map_timer_htu_maps_desc: Use the buttons at the top to switch between Groudon, Kyogre and Rayquaza maps. The timer and all spawns reset automatically.
map_timer_htu_timer_desc: Press ▶ Play to start the countdown from 10:00. You can also drag the slider, or click the minutes/seconds fields to jump to any time.
map_timer_htu_spawns_desc: Pokemon icons appear on the map at the correct game time. Click an icon to mark it as defeated - it will grey out or disappear and its respawn timer will start automatically.
map_timer_htu_towers_desc: Click a goal zone to mark it as destroyed. Some Pokemon only appear (or disappear) depending on which goals are broken, so keep them updated for accurate timings.
map_timer_htu_tooltip_desc: Hover over any Pokemon or goal zone icon for about 1 second to see detailed information: HP, spawn rules, and special interactions.
map_timer_htu_reset_desc: Switching maps or pressing the map button again resets everything to the start of the game.

stream_step1_desc: Before selecting a Pokemon, click 🟣 Purple or 🟠 Orange to assign picks to the right team. If no team is selected, the Pokemon will be added without a colored border.
stream_step2_desc: Click on Pokemon cards in the right list. They appear in the left panel with the active team's border color. Click again to remove them.
stream_step3_desc: In the ⛔ Bans tab, choose the ban order: Purple first (P-O-P-O-P-O), Orange first (O-P-O-P-O-P), or Free (3 Purple then 3 Orange automatically). Click Pokemon to ban them — the team color is assigned automatically. Use the '+ Empty ban' card to add a ban without showing a Pokemon.
stream_step4_desc: Choose the match map at the bottom of the left panel: Rayquaza, Groudon or Kyogre. The selected map is shown in its own dedicated Map Overlay.
stream_step5_intro: You need to create four Browser Sources in OBS:
stream_step5_controller_desc: the main control window (keep open, but off-stream)
stream_step5_map_desc: shows only the selected map, great for placing it anywhere on your OBS scene independently
stream_step6_desc:
• Controller: ~460 × 700 px (not in stream)
• Picks Overlay: ~750 × 220 px
• Bans Overlay: ~580 × 180 px
• Map Overlay: ~380 × 120 px
stream_step7_desc: For each Browser Source, check "Remove background color" (or add Custom CSS: body { background-color: rgba(0,0,0,0) !important; }) so the overlays blend cleanly over your stream scene.
stream_tip: 💡 Tip: The 📺 PICKS OBS, ⛔ BANS OBS and 🗺️ MAP OBS buttons open each overlay window at the right size. The ✕ CLEAR button resets everything (picks, bans and map).

xpcalc_desc: Simulate XP gain across every camp and objective. Find the optimal farming path to hit your level spikes before key fights.
xpcalc_team_config_hint: Configure your Ally (Exp. Share) and the Enemy (Catch-Up Modifier + parallel simulation)
xpcalc_ally_preset_label: Assign a Farm Preset to the ally track
xpcalc_ally_preset_hint: The ally will follow this Kill Queue in parallel during Advanced Simulation. Their live XP determines Exp. Share eligibility each tick.
xpcalc_enemy_level_label: Highest level on the opposing team (Catch-Up reference)
xpcalc_enemy_preset_label: Assign a Farm Preset to the enemy track
xpcalc_enemy_preset_hint: The enemy will follow this Kill Queue in Advanced Simulation. Their live level updates the Catch-Up modifier in real time.
xpcalc_preset_empty_hint: No presets yet. Build a queue and save it!
xpcalc_empty_queue_hint: Add wild Pokémon kills, player KOs or scoring events below.
xpcalc_credits_intro: The data used in this calculator comes from the Mathcord community. Many thanks to all contributors!
xpcalc_catchup_warn_text: Applying the Catch-Up Modifier to Player KOs is not yet confirmed in-game. This value is a theoretical estimate based on the general mechanic.
xpcalc_howto_step1: Choose your Pokémon and set your starting level.
xpcalc_howto_step2: Set the Start Timer (when you start farming) of your session.
xpcalc_howto_step3: Configure the Enemy Team section - set the highest enemy Pokémon level to activate the Catch-Up Modifier if applicable.
xpcalc_howto_step4: Add kills from the Wild Pokémon grid. Click a Pokémon, set the timer and number of allies sharing XP, then confirm.
xpcalc_howto_step5: Add Player KO events via the Kill Queue panel - enter the victim's level, their streak, and whether you landed the killing blow.
xpcalc_howto_step6: Add Scoring events using the scoring quick-add row (timer + points scored).
xpcalc_howto_step7: Press Classic for an instant summary, or Advanced to watch a real-time simulation that you can speed up to x4.
xpcalc_howto_tip: The XP Table at the bottom shows how much XP each wild Pokémon gives at every timer tick - use it to plan kills efficiently.
xpcalc_howto_footnote:
Passive XP: Automatic - 4 XP/sec between 10:00 and 8:00, then 6 XP/sec between 8:00 and 0:00.
XP Share: Coming Soon - will be implemented in a future update.
Catch-Up on Player KO: Unconfirmed - enable the option at your own risk to test the theoretical value.
xpcalc_disclaimer_intro: This calculator is an estimation tool designed to approximate Pokémon UNITE's in-game mechanics as closely as possible. It does not claim to perfectly reproduce every match condition.
xpcalc_disclaimer_data_body: XP values for wild Pokémon, passive XP, scoring, and KOs are based on in-game observations and measurements. They may differ slightly depending on the game version, balance updates, or undocumented conditions.
xpcalc_disclaimer_partial_body: Some mechanics - in particular the application of the Catch-Up Modifier to Player KOs - are not officially documented by the developers and have not yet been exhaustively verified in-game. The corresponding values are theoretical extrapolations.
xpcalc_disclaimer_model_body: This simulator does not reproduce every condition of a real match: Pokémon interactions, exact wild respawn timing, Exp. Share between nearby allies, held item buffs, and other situational factors are not yet integrated.
xpcalc_disclaimer_dev_body: This tool is actively developed. Data is updated as patches are released. If you spot an inconsistency or have data to share, feel free to contribute.
xpcalc_disclaimer_footer: This calculator is an independent community project, unaffiliated with TiMi Studio Group, Nintendo, or The Pokémon Company.
xpcalc_roadmap_intro: Here are the features currently in development or planned for upcoming versions of the XP Calculator.
xpcalc_roadmap_item_desc: Continuous refinement of all data: wild Pokémon respawn timing, held item buffs, player KO formulas, Catch-Up Modifier verification on KOs. Community contributions from Mathcord are always welcome.
xpcalc_roadmap_footer: Have an idea, data to share or found a bug? Open a ticket in the Feedback part and contribute to the project!
